resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Bloomingdale Construction Department (Construction Official; inspection by the CCO Officer)
requirements: Smoke alarms on each level including the basement, outside bedroom areas, and in the laundry room over the dryer
Battery-only smoke and CO alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units (UL listed); hardwired alarms must not be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarms (hardwired too) over 10 years old must be replaced; CO alarms replaced at end of life
Carbon monoxide alarm near the sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage

Secondary power source label (for example CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and electric meter if the home has a generator, solar panels or battery storage
House number on the house, 4 to 12 inches high
Graspable handrails on steps with four or more risers
Guardrails (at least 36 inches) on porches and stoops more than 30 inches above grade
GFCI outlets within 6 feet of any water source inside and on all outside outlets
No double-cylinder (keyed both sides) lock on the front entrance door
All bedroom windows open and close easily
Door from an attached garage into the house must be 20-minute fire rated (steel, 1 3/8 inch solid wood or sheet metal on the garage side, no glass)
Heating and water heater flue pipes in good repair and sealed to the chimney; relief valves piped to within 6 inches of the floor
Decks in good condition and to NJ building code; pools (24 inches or deeper) to code and zoning
Accessory structures in good repair and zoning compliant; yard clean and free of rubbish

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's residential Continued Certificate of Occupancy application completely (check Resale), and submit it with the $200 fee to the Construction Department, 182 Union Avenue. The CCO Officer (Mark Lime) then contacts you to schedule the inspection, or you can call or email him for an appointment. Per Borough Ordinance 11-1.6(g), payment must be cash or cashier's check payable to the Borough of Bloomingdale.
resale_co.contact_title: CCO Officer (Construction and Zoning Official: Leonard Perre, 973-838-7995, constructionofficial@bloomingdalenj.net)

Requirements for obtaining a Certificate of Continued Occupancy. Mark Lime the CCO Officer will contact you to schedule the inspection.

Fill out the application completely. Submit it with your  check for $200.00 for single -family dwellings and/or commercial property. Cash, personal check or certified bank check made out to the Borough of Bloomingdale is all that is accepted.

resale_co.notes: Bloomingdale requires a Continued Certificate of Occupancy when a home is sold (Section 11-1.6). The residential form is also used for refinances when the bank requires one. Fee: the ordinance sets $200 for a residential single-family dwelling and $100 per unit for multifamily or residential rental units; the residential form says $200.00 per dwelling. The fee for selling an owner-occupied two-family home is not spelled out (could be $200 per dwelling or $100 per unit); confirm with the office. Payment method conflict: the 2021 checklist accepts cash, personal check or certified bank check, but the ordinance and the current Building Department page say cash or cashier's check only; use cash or cashier's check. The ordinance file on the Borough site is the clean introduced version of Ordinance 24-2023; the Building Department page cites Section 11-1.6(G), which matches it. The ordinance lets the Construction Official waive the inspection and fee if the same premises were inspected within the last 60 days with no physical change. Bloomingdale's Construction Department also serves Butler and Kinnelon. The form asks about secondary power sources, abandoned wells, septic or fuel tanks, and permits issued in the last five years. Rental properties are separate: non owner-occupied 1-2 family rentals must register yearly with the Municipal Clerk ($150.00 per unit), and rentals need a lead paint inspection; tenant changes use the separate rental CCO application ($100.00 per dwelling or unit).

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level including the basement, outside bedroom areas, and in the laundry room over the dryer (Borough CCO checklist)
Battery-only smoke and CO alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units, UL listed
Hardwired smoke alarms must not be over 10 years old and must not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm near the sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage
Secondary power source label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and electric meter for homes with a generator, solar panels or battery storage (printed, not handwritten)

authorities.name: Bloomingdale Fire Prevention Bureau (Bloomingdale Fire Department, local enforcing agency); smoke detector inspections are scheduled through the Building Department
authorities.how_to_apply: The Fire Prevention Bureau page says smoke detector inspections go through the Building Department (973-838-7995). The Borough's resale CCO inspection by Mark Lime (who is also the Fire Official) checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the secondary power label. Call the Building Department to confirm whether the CCO covers the smoke and CO certificate or a separate application and fee are needed.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA registry lists the Bloomingdale Fire Department as the fire code enforcing agency. The Borough's Fire Prevention Bureau page sends smoke detector inspections to the Building Department, and Mark Lime is both the Fire Official and the CCO Officer, so the resale CCO inspection appears to double as the smoke and CO alarm check. No separate published fee for the smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and secondary power source certificate was found on the Borough site; confirm by phone. The Fire Prevention Bureau email appears two ways on Borough pages (fireprevention@bloomingdalenj.net on the Bureau page, bfprevention@optonline.net on the Fire Department page and in the state directory); the Borough-domain address is used here. The Fire Prevention Bureau permit form lists a cell number for the Fire Official, which is not used. The CCO application still lists an extinguisher among the fire safety equipment questions but the checklist does not require one.

other_items.label: Open permits and approvals
other_items.detail: The CCO application asks for construction permits issued in the last five years and any Planning Board or Board of Adjustment approvals; the office checks for open permits.

other_items.label: Abandoned wells, septic or fuel tanks
other_items.detail: The CCO application asks whether there are any abandoned wells, septic systems or fuel tanks on the property.
